exposure: wide opening of the vesicouterine space
removal of the dehiscent cesarean scar and all intrauterine abnormal fibrous tissues
intramyometrial injection of autologous platelet-rich plasma
cohort: 54 patients aged 25-41 with recurrent large cesarean scar defects
finding: Comprehensive repair of recurrent low-large hysterotomy defects using a myometrial glide flap was associated with a high rate of successful pregnancies and deliveries, with no cases of placenta previa, dehiscence, placenta accreta spectrum, or postpartum hemorrhage.
mod_finding: All 12 patients who became pregnant again delivered by cesarean between 36.1 and 38.0 weeks.
